title: Taskflow Agent finds missing OAuth state validation in Lobsters Mastodon linking
summary: The Mastodon OAuth callback lacked state validation and session binding, allowing a cross-site request forgery that could link a victim’s Lobsters account to an attacker-controlled Mastodon account.
ai_role: GHSL credits its Taskflow Agent and manual verification by Peter Stöckli and Man Yue Mo. Reported 2025-12-09; fixed on main branch 2025-12-22. The maintainer reported a collision with another report; priority/originality is therefore not exclusive. No CVE is listed.
classification_note: The advisory limits exposure to Lobsters instances with Mastodon linking enabled and notes the reported collision; no in-the-wild claim is made.
remediation_note: GHSL reports fixes on main branch in commits 9a29bba and 41d6d02 on 2025-12-22. No tagged release or CVE is given.

impacts.conditions: The CSRF flaw lets an attacker link a Mastodon profile to a victim’s Lobsters profile; the source says further impact is only possible if the integration expands. This is a profile-link change and an authorization-control bypass, not authentication bypass.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes the vulnerability and PoC; it does not establish exploitation in the wild.
